creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The canonical null-guard fires a false positive:

    if a != null and len(a) > 3:      // RAD30001 on `a`: str? into str|list|map
    if b == null or len(b) > 3:       // same
    if type_of(c) != "str" or len(c) > 3:   // same

In each case the left operand proves the right operand safe, which is the
whole point of writing it that way. `x != null and <use x>` is about the
most common defensive idiom there is, so this is a steady source of noise
on correct code.

Found while landing `stop-the-checker` (a_25Nhy9Un4). After that card's
fixes, a sweep of 62 real scripts had 11 diagnostics left - 9 of them were
this, all in one script, all from one `or` chain. It is now the single
biggest remaining source of checker noise on real code.

### Root cause

The narrowing logic is already correct; the synthesis pass just doesn't
use it. Two passes run over an if-condition, and only one of them knows
about short-circuiting:

- `interpretAnd` / `interpretOr` (`rts/check/narrow.go:220`, `:237`)
  build the right-hand frame properly - `frame.WithMany(leftRef.WhenTrue)`
  for `and`, `.WhenFalse` for `or` - and the doc comment there spells the
  intent out: "in `x != null and x > 5`, the `x > 5` is evaluated knowing
  x is non-null".
- `synthOpBinary` (`rts/check/type_check.go:3502`) does
  `left := tc.synth(n.Left); right := tc.synth(n.Right)` - both under the
  same `tc.frame`, with no notion of short-circuiting.

`walkIf` (`type_check.go:859-860`) synths the whole condition first and
interprets it second. Diagnostics come from synthesis, so the narrowing
that interpretation computes never reaches the operand that needed it.

### Likely shape of the fix

Special-case `rl.OpAnd` / `rl.OpOr` in `synthOpBinary`: interpret the left operand, then synth the right under
the left's WhenTrue (and) / WhenFalse (or) frame, restoring after. That
mirrors `interpretAnd`/`interpretOr` rather than inventing a second rule,
and the two should probably share a helper so they can't drift.

Watch for the ordering: `interpretCondition` calls `synth` on sub-nodes in
places, so check there's no re-entrancy problem between the two passes,
and that `ExprTypes` ends up recording the narrowed type (hover should
show `str`, not `str?`, over the `a` in `len(a)`).

### Done when

- All three shapes above check clean.
- Negative case pinned: the narrowing must NOT leak to the operand that
  doesn't get it - `if len(a) > 3 and a != null:` (guard written second)
  still reports, because there the use genuinely isn't protected.
- A case under `rts/check/snapshots/narrow/`.
title: Short-circuit and/or doesn't narrow its later operands
